verses.text: Then the LORD said to Moses, "Come up to the LORD, you and Aaron, Nadab and Abihu, and seventy of the leaders of Israel. Worship from a distance.
Only Moses may come near the LORD. The others must not come near, and the people must not come up with him."
Moses went and told the people all the LORD's words and laws. They all answered with one voice, "We will do everything the LORD has said."
Then Moses wrote down everything the LORD had said. Early the next morning he got up and built an altar at the foot of the mountain. He set up twelve stone pillars for the twelve tribes of Israel.
Then he sent young men of Israel, and they offered burnt offerings and sacrificed young bulls as peace offerings to the LORD.
Moses took half of the blood and put it in bowls, and the other half he sprinkled on the altar.
Then he took the Book of the Covenant and read it aloud to the people. They said, "We will do everything the LORD has said. We will obey."
Then Moses took the blood and sprinkled it on the people. He said, "This is the blood of the covenant the LORD has made with you, based on all these words."
Then Moses and Aaron, Nadab and Abihu, and seventy of the leaders of Israel went up the mountain.
They saw the God of Israel. Under his feet was something like a floor made of sapphire stones, as clear as the sky itself.
God did not raise his hand against these leaders of Israel. They saw God, and they ate and drank.
The LORD said to Moses, "Come up to me on the mountain and stay here. I will give you the stone tablets with the law and commands I have written for teaching the people."
So Moses set out with Joshua his helper, and Moses went up the mountain of God.
He said to the leaders, "Wait here for us until we come back to you. Aaron and Hur are with you. Anyone who has a dispute can go to them."
When Moses went up the mountain, the cloud covered it.
The glory of the LORD settled on Mount Sinai. For six days the cloud covered the mountain. On the seventh day the LORD called to Moses from inside the cloud.
To the people of Israel, the glory of the LORD looked like a burning fire on top of the mountain.
Then Moses went into the cloud as he climbed up the mountain. And he stayed on the mountain forty days and forty nights.
